name: 2-Block Littlestone Dimension
definition: The **2-Block Littlestone Dimension** $\mathrm{B}_2(\mathcal{H})$ is the largest depth of a complete binary tree shattered by $\mathcal{H}$ in which, in every block of two consecutive levels, the first level is unrestricted and the two nodes on the second level have the same domain-point label. Equivalently, each block asks two coordinates before receiving their two labels, giving four branches, and successive blocks may depend on all preceding labels.
graph_summary: Maximum total query depth of a shattered tree whose two-coordinate batches are fixed before their labels are revealed.
description: Database-defined structural variant; no published origin is claimed.

monotonic.proof: A constrained shattered tree for a subfamily is still shattered by every containing class, with exactly the same block-label constraints.

p_monotonic.proof: Every coordinate queried by a shattered tree for a projection is retained.  Lift, for each leaf, a projected realizing hypothesis to an original hypothesis; the same tree is then shattered before projection and retains its block constraints.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, so it cannot create a larger constrained shattered tree.
